evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2020-01-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2020-01-01". A POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain YYYY-MM-DD string with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2019-05-05"} returned 200 and the new date. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null. PATCH /todos/3 with null cleared it the same way, and I then set it back.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "01/02/2026", "2026-13-01", "abc", the number 20260101, "2026-1-1" and "" each returned 400 with the error 'dueDate must be a YYYY-MM-DD calendar date'. PATCH with "2026-02-30" also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-11-01. I created these todos: past due (2020-01-01), future due (2030-01-01), due today (2026-11-01), no due date, and done with a past due date. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past-due, not-done todo. The no-date, done, future and due-today todos were excluded. The overdue field in the responses matched.
evidence.AC5: The page at / showed each due date as '(fällig 2020-01-01)', '(fällig 2030-01-01)' and so on. The todo with no due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot only the past-due, not-done todo had 'überfällig' appended. The future, due-today, no-date and done-past-due todos did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a button labelled 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it reduced the list from 5 items to 1, the overdue 'past' todo.
